sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203].
Operating income grew faster at 12.3% and net income at 14.7%, so margins widened modestly across the window [F204][F205].
FY2021 was the first inflection, with revenue up 17.5% on a 16% comparable sales increase and strong non-foods and e-commerce [D189][P56].
FY2022 added another 15.8%, driven by a 14% comparable sales gain and inflation, with gasoline and travel strongest [D238][P42].
Growth then stepped down to 6.8% in FY2023 and 5.0% in FY2024 before recovering to 8.2% and 10.1% in the last two years [D287][D336][D385][D434].
The US segment supplied 7.2pp of FY2026's 10.1% revenue growth, with Other International adding 1.6pp and Canada 1.3pp [D672][D679][D686][D434].
FY2026 net sales rose $27.3 billion, primarily on an 8% comparable sales increase from 5% higher average ticket and 3% more shopping frequency [P14].
Food and Sundries remains the largest product line at 38.5% of revenue but contributed only 2.6pp of growth, while warehouse ancillary contributed 3.7pp [D558][D560][D601].
Membership fees grew 11.0% to $5.9 billion on new sign-ups, fee increases and Executive upgrades [D664][S78][P13].
Operating income grew 12.5% against 10.1% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 4.7%, so profit outran the top line [D435][D434][D457].
Operating margin reached 3.9% in FY2026, a window high against a 3.4% median and 3.1% low [F32][D691][D692][D690].
The FY2026 gain was only 0.1pp, with SG&A adding 0.1pp and cost of revenue flat [D447][D460][D459].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of sales, though excluding gasoline inflation it rose one basis point, with currency adding $126 million of expense [P9].
Gross margin slipped three basis points as faster-growing ancillary sales shifted mix, partly offset by IEEPA tariff refunds worth three basis points [P12].
Net margin of 3.0% sits below the 3.5% retail peer median, and the 24.7% tax rate is close to prior years [F52][D712][D420].
Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income, and free cash flow of $9.4 billion was 1.02x, above the 0.99x window median [F82][F42][D421][F102][D422][D701].
The FY2026 operating cash increase came from higher operating income and a smaller inventory investment on faster turns and better supplier terms [P6].
Capex of $6.4 billion was 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A, the highest multiple in the window [F92][F10][D417][D423].
Free cash flow margin of 3.1% is above the 2.8% median but below the 4.2% peer median [D418][D698][D714].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion, or 5.0% of revenue, the 100th percentile against six retail peers whose median is -4.4% [D427][D428][D715][D716].
Long-term debt fell 31.5% to $3.9 billion while cash and investments rose 39.4% to $21.3 billion [D445][F192][D453][D425].
Buybacks and dividends of $3.3 billion consumed 35.2% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count was essentially flat at 444.4 million [D429][D430][X100].
FY2026 repurchases of 891,000 shares cost $847 million, leaving $1.1 billion under the January 2023 authorization [P3].
Operating margin of 3.9% ranks in the 17th percentile of six retail peers against a 5.0% median, a structural thin-margin position rather than a deterioration [F32][D709][D710].
Capex has grown 17.0% in FY2026 and capex/D&A has climbed to 2.41x, so free cash flow depends on continued operating cash growth [D441][D423].
Receivables grew 23.6% in FY2026, faster than the 10.1% revenue growth, though days sales outstanding only moved to 5 days [D455][D434][D431].
If FY2027 operating margin holds at or above the FY2026 3.9% high, the multi-year widening trend is intact; a drop toward the 3.4% median would reverse it [F32][D691][D692].
Free cash flow conversion of 1.02x net income should stay above the 0.99x median; a fall toward the 0.60x FY2022 low would signal working-capital or capex strain [D422][D701][D699].
Watch net cash as a share of revenue, now 5.0%; a move back toward the 2.1% FY2024 level would mark heavier capital deployment [D428][D330].
